page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, delivering dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench text processing scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core operations, static web serving throughput at 11.2 GB/sec, and software compilation align with mid-range averages. However, memory bandwidth presents a notable bottleneck; while cached small-block reads are average, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths fall into the weak and poor categories respectively, indicating potential performance degradation during memory-intensive, out-of-cache operations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c3d-highcpu-8 offers a dense compute-to-RAM ratio suitable for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration enhances its utility for specific mathematical and secure workloads. This profile is well-suited for workloads such as web serving, text processing, lightweight build compilation, and moderate computational tasks, though it is less optimal for memory-bound databases or large-scale LLM inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor with dedicated CPU allocation. It provides 4 physical cores with multithreading, 32 MB of L3 cache, and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show strong single-core capabilities, particularly in text processing and stress-ng tests, while multi-core execution and web serving throughput remain average. A key hardware tradeoff is its memory subsystem, which exhibits poor uncached large-block write bandwidth. Given its 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU ratio and support for AVX-512 and cryptographic instructions, this instance is best suited for compute-bound workloads, text processing, and web serving rather than memory-intensive applications.
